common_name: Maui Picture-Winged Fly (Band-Winged Lek Display & Foretarsal Ciliation)

chronoseries.what_changes: Geological age stays 0 Ma. The selected Turing wavelength collapses from the obscura-group primordium scale (117 µm predecessor, 114 µm successor) to the planitibia detail-tier pigment wavelength 5.13 µm. At fixed Schnakenberg kinetics and diffusion ratio, activator diffusivity scales as lambda^2.

scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength on the Drosophila planitibia wing membrane (detail scale)

equations.pde: du/dt = D_u laplacian(u) + rho (a - u + u^2 v); dv/dt = D_v laplacian(v) + rho (b - u^2 v)
equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = max Re eig([[rho f_u - D_u k^2, rho f_v], [rho g_u, rho g_v - D_v k^2]])
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = rho (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v); lambda_c = 2 pi / k_star where k_star = argmax sigma(k)
equations.turing_threshold: D_v f_u + D_u g_v > 0 and (D_v f_u + D_u g_v)^2 > 4 D_u D_v det(J), with trace(J) < 0 and det(J) > 0
equations.boundary_conditions: periodic square patch of wing membrane; no-flux is equivalent for the discrete Fourier modes used to measure sigma(k)

parameters.note: d = D_v/D_u = 18.6 is specific to slot 3199. It is not the power-law alpha/beta used by the 197 µm planitibia sibling or the 117 µm persimilis sibling. Nominal gamma and dx are chosen in the script so the fastest linear mode sits at 5.13 µm.

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) gives the dispersion relation that selects a finite critical wavenumber when the inhibitor diffuses farther than the activator.
Schnakenberg (1979) supplies the two-species kinetics a - u + u^2 v and b - u^2 v used here.

Edwards, Doescher, Kaneshiro and Yamamoto (2007) published the Hawaiian Drosophila wing-diversity database that documents picture-wing pigment patterns, including the planitibia group. They do not report a 5.13 µm wavelength.

Kambysellis et al. (1995, Current Biology 5:1129) place Hawaiian picture-winged Drosophila, including the planitibia radiation, in a molecular phylogeny of ecological shifts. The DOI 10.1073/pnas.92.17.7819 is a different 1995 PNAS paper and is not this source.

Carson (1982) describes the radiation of Drosophila on the newer Hawaiian volcanoes (Maui planitibia group included). Carson (1997) treats sexual selection, the biological context of the band-winged lek.
The assigned phenomenon scale for this detail variant is 5.13e-06 m (5.1 µm, log10 = -5.290) at geological age 0 Ma.
